title: Halcyon Financial POC: Sprint Briefing & Risk Radar
content:
TL;DR:
- Customer: Halcyon Financial (regulated payments fintech). Goal: validate Redwood Private deployment (VPC+HSM) for real-time transaction enrichment and compliance-safe redaction.
- Sprint: 3 weeks + 1-week buffer. Main success metrics: p95 latency <= 180ms on standard queries, end-to-end throughput 75 req/s steady-state, model output F1 >= 0.92 on labeled redaction tests, and zero PII escapes in 10k synthetic test corpus.

Objective & hypothesis:
- Objective: Prove Redwood Private can be provisioned into Halcyon's AWS account, integrate with their KMS-backed key material, and serve inference for the enrichment microservice with predictable latency and audit logs.
- Hypothesis: With dedicated small-GPU pool + prefix cache we can meet latency and cost SLOs; if not, canary fallback to hosted API for spike protection.

Primary success criteria (pass/fail):
1) Performance: p95 response time <= 180ms for 16-token prompts and model variant rwd-7b-q4f on same-VPC GPUs under 75 req/s sustained for 30m.
2) Functional: Redaction test suite (10k synthetic records) must have 0 PII leaks; measured by automated regex + human spot-check (20 samples).
3) Throughput & stability: Sustained 75 req/s with <1% errors over a 1-hour soak.
4) Observability: Trace-level logs available in Halcyon's splunk/kinesis endpoint; cost + token breakdown shows expected unit cost within 15% of demo projection.

Secondary criteria (informational):
- Latency tail under adversarial sequences (2x typical length) and cold-start behavior for first-request after scale-down.
- Operator ergonomics: rollout via Redwood Console works end-to-end and team can trigger rollback.

In-scope / Out-of-scope (short):
- In-scope: Private control plane deployment into Halcyon AWS account (VPC peering), KMS integration, sample enrichment pipeline integration (REST), basic eval harness and dashboards, one canary policy.
- Out-of-scope: Full production dataset onboarding, legal review of long-term data retention, advanced autoscaling policies beyond our default, integration with Halcyon's internal customer portal.

Kickoff workshop agenda (90 minutes) — proposed for Week 0:
- 00–10m: Intros + success criteria review (Maya)
- 10–30m: Network & security constraints (Halcyon infra lead) — discuss subnets, egress restrictions, TLS termination, proxy requirements
- 30–50m: Key management & audit logs (Priya) — KMS/HSM mapping, rotation, and RBAC plan
- 50–70m: Integration plan for enrichment service (Liam) — REST contract, error semantics, retries, header expectations
- 70–80m: Test harness & dataset plan (Ethan) — synthetic corpus, redaction test design, labeling rules
- 80–90m: Next steps, ownership, blockers (Maya)

Timeline & milestones (high level):
- Week 0 (Kickoff + infra access): Network/VPN access, IAM role provisioning, KMS test key created
- Week 1 (Provisioning + integration): Private control plane deploy, GPU pool boot, test endpoint reachable inside VPC, basic API smoke tests
- Week 2 (Load & function): Run soak tests, run redaction suite, iteratively tune batching/cache settings, begin dashboards
- Week 3 (Acceptance): Final acceptance run, docs handover, runbook + oncall brief, delivery demo for Halcyon PMs
- Buffer week: rollback plan & small fixes if criteria not met

Risk Radar (likelihood x impact notes):
- Network constraints (High likelihood / High impact): Corporate egress restrictions may block outbound telemetry. Mitigation: prepare an offline syslog delivery mode and pre-approved IP ranges; request firewall test window in kickoff.
- KMS policy friction (Medium / High): Customer KMS policies may prevent our test key usage. Mitigation: use temporary dedicated key and document rotation; include security contact in day-0 checklist.
- Dataset sensitivity (Medium / Medium): Synthetic tests may miss edge PII cases. Mitigation: expand regex patterns; schedule 1-2 human reviews and escalate to product ML.
- Resource contention (Low / Medium): Limited GPU capacity in their account or quotas. Mitigation: propose small instance footprint and timeboxed soak; fallback to hosted for spikes.
- Observability blackout (Low / High): Agent/collector blocked by network. Mitigation: provide agentless log push via S3 presigned object as fallback.

Data & security checklist (must be green before Week 1):
- IAM role with least privilege created and shared (ARN)
- VPC peering or Transit Gateway details + test route table entries
- Test KMS key with policy allowing Redwood SP role (temporary)
- Egress rules and approved outbound IPs for telemetry and CRL checks
- Data retention window defined for POC logs (default 30d)
- NDA + DPA countersigned (legal) — status: Halcyon legal awaiting signature (action: Maya)

Measurement plan / telemetry specs:
- Metrics to publish to Halcyon watchers: request_count, success_rate, latency_p50/p95/p99, tokens_in/tokens_out, cost_per_1k_tokens_estimate
- Alerts: error_rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m, latency_p95 > 250ms for 10m, PII-detection-failure > 0 (critical)
- Dashboards: one per route + model variant, token-cost heatmap, canary rollout timeline

Deployment & canary strategy (notes):
- Deploy model variant rwd-7b-q4f in Redwood Private pool in Halcyon's VPC.
- Canary policy: route 5% traffic for 30 minutes -> 25% for 2 hours -> 100% if no regressions.
- Rollback: immediate fallback to hosted rwd-7b (with redaction shim) if PII leakage or latency regressions observed. Documented rollback playbook in /runbooks/halcyon-poc.md (GH PR will add).

Acceptance tests (automation):
- redaction_suite.sh -> runs 10k synthetic documents through endpoint, checks for regex escapes and outputs summary CSV
- perf_soak.py -> drives 75 req/s for 1 hour, captures latency percentiles and error traces to S3
- trace_validation -> compares trace IDs in Redwood Console and Halcyon Splunk ingestion to validate end-to-end trace propagation

Resource matrix & contacts:
- Customer PM: Rebecca Li (Halcyon) — product acceptance lead
- Customer Infra: Omar Reyes (Halcyon) — VPC/IAM contact
- Redwood SE lead: Maya Chen (owner) — sprint steering
- Redwood infra eng: Liam O'Connor — provisioning + network
- Redwood security/crypto: Priya Singh — KMS & compliance
- Redwood performance: Ethan Park — load harness & tuning
- Escalation (internal): Jordan Alvarez (SRE lead) — pager if tests fail in acceptance window

Open questions / decisions needed (by Week 0 kickoff):
- Can Halcyon create a temporary test KMS key and allow Redwood SP role? (open, Halcyon security)
- Which telemetry endpoint is the primary sink (Splunk or Kinesis)? (open, Halcyon infra)
- Are there specific reject/obfuscation rules beyond PCI/SSN/EMAIL we must encode for PII? Provide list. (open, Halcyon compliance)
- Acceptance definition for cost (how tight is the +15% budget tolerance?). (open, Halcyon PM)

Notes to self / workshop prep TODOs:
- Prepare a minimal Terraform sketch for VPC peering and role attachment (Liam)
- Bring replayable synthetic corpus (Ethan) and quick instructions for manual spot-checkers
- Draft short legal checklist to accelerate signature (Maya)
- Pre-seed dashboard templates and alert rules (Priya)

Next steps (immediate):
1) Confirm kickoff date/time with Halcyon (Maya)
2) Halcyon to share IAM role ARN + KMS test key by Day -1
3) Redwood to provision Private CP and return smoke endpoint (Liam)
4) Run first smoke tests and share results in Slack thread linked above

Unresolved: this doc intentionally keeps acceptance numeric thresholds conservative — revisit after Week 1 soak and update runbook.

Appendix: quick checklist for demo day
- Demo flow: request->trace->redaction check->dashboard cost panel->handover runbook
- Show fallback working (hosted fallback triggered manually)
- Prepare short slide with risk mitigation commitments and next-phase options (Dedicated or long-term Private).

(End of sprint briefing)
